{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2009–10 |team=New Mexico State Aggies |image=New Mexico State Aggies wordmark.svg |conference=Western Athletic Conference |division= |short_conf= WAC |CoachRank= |APRank= |record=22–12 |conf_record=11–5 |head_coach=[[Marvin Menzies]] |hc_year=3rd |asst_coach1= [[Mick Durham]] |asst_coach2=Chris Pompey |asst_coach3= [[Paul Weir (basketball)|Paul Weir]] |stadium=[[Pan American Center]] |champion=WAC Tournament Champions |bowl=[[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result=Round of 64 }} {{2009–10 WAC men's basketball standings}} The '''2009–10 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team''' represented [[New Mexico State University]] in the [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]] [[college basketball]] season. This was [[Marvin Menzies]] 3rd season as head coach. The Aggies played their home games at the [[Pan American Center]] and competed in the [[2009–10 WAC men's basketball season|Western Athletic Conference]]. They finished the season 22–12, 11–5 in WAC play. They won the [[2010 WAC men's basketball tournament]] to earn the conference's automatic bid to the [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. They earned a 12 seed in the Midwest Region where they were defeated by a 5 seed and AP #13 [[2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] in the first round. ==Pre-season== In the WAC preseason polls, released October 20 via media teleconference{{Cite web |url=http://www.wacsports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=45988&SPID=4126&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=10100&ATCLID=204817316 |title = 2009-10 WAC Basketball Preseason Polls Announced - WACSports.com Official Web Site of the Western Athletic Conference |access-date=2009-12-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120225130154/http://www.wacsports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=45988&SPID=4126&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=10100&ATCLID=204817316 |archive-date=2012-02-25 |url-status=dead }} New Mexico State was selected to finish 3rd in the coaches and media poll.
